articles.title: Lakes aren't just storing water—they're changing the carbon cycle
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Lakes may look like picturesque stopping points along a river or stream, but they can have a big influence on what happens to carbon as it moves through a landscape. New research suggests that the more lake-rich a network of streams is, the more carbon is released into the atmosphere rather than carried downstream.

articles.title: Ocean indicators NOAA scientists are tracking for El Niño's arrival on the West Coast
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Has El Niño reached the West Coast? You might think it has. After all, the ocean off Southern and Central California is unusually warm. But that warmth is from a recent marine heat wave that predates the current El Niño. Much of the Pacific Coast is experiencing relatively normal conditions while still awaiting the impacts of what could be a very strong El Niño.

articles.title: Life uses 4 DNA letters. Scientists just made 8 work
articles.summary: Researchers at UC San Diego have demonstrated that a key cellular enzyme can accurately read an eight-letter genetic alphabet, doubling the four letters used by all known life on Earth. Detailed imaging revealed that RNA polymerase handles synthetic DNA letters in surprisingly similar ways to natural ones. The finding brings scientists closer to building expanded genetic systems that could perform entirely new biological functions.
